source: The maintainer's answer of 2026-11-24 (a logout after a tenant switch ends the login it came from too); RFC 0009 §11.4 (sentences proposed in the PR)
statement: Logging out of a session a tenant switch started ends the login it was switched from (its root, IDN-36) as well, through every logout of CoSec's revoker: TokenRevoker.revoke of the access token, of the pair, and the served logout route (IDN-24); the root is read from the session's record, so the access token alone suffices. The root is revoked first, then the session, then the token's id, each by a conditional write, so a refresh or a switch that read the root before cannot write it back live, and a logout that fails at a step has done none of the later ones: it is answered as a failure (503 when the store cannot read or write), never as done while the login lives on, and its retry starts again. A root already revoked or gone is left as it is, a root of another principal is left alone and logged, and a login's own logout ends only itself. A switched session whose record is gone (pushed out of its principal's latest sessions in its tenant, IDN-35) cannot find its root. The access tokens the root and the other sessions switched from it issued stay valid until they expire, and those sessions end at their next refresh or switch.
